candidates.title: Estimating cumulative point prevalence of rare diseases: analysis of the Orphanet database
candidates.summary: Analysis of Orphanet prevalence data estimating that rare diseases together affect 3.5-5.9% of the population (263-446 million people).
candidates.reason: Establishes the scale of the rare-disease burden for the introduction hook.

candidates.title: Time to diagnosis and determinants of diagnostic delays of people living with a rare disease: results of a Rare Barometer retrospective patient survey
candidates.summary: European patient survey estimating an average total diagnosis time of close to five years for people with a rare disease, with longer delays for women and children.
candidates.reason: Quantifies the cost of diagnostic delay that motivates closing the literature-database gap.

candidates.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of GFAP gene variants in Alexander disease
candidates.summary: Systematic review of 186 papers identifying 550 Alexander disease participants carrying 182 different causative GFAP variants.
candidates.reason: Source of the corrected Alexander disease hook figures (550 patients, 182 variants).

candidates.title: ClinVar: improving access to variant interpretations and supporting evidence
candidates.summary: Describes ClinVar as a public archive of submitted interpretations of human variants and their relationship to disease.
candidates.reason: Canonical ClinVar reference; ClinVar holds only what submitters deposit, which defines the gap.

candidates.title: ClinVar: updates to support classifications of both germline and somatic variants
candidates.summary: Recent ClinVar update describing support for germline and somatic classifications.
candidates.reason: Current ClinVar reference used as ground truth and submission target.

candidates.title: OMIM.org: leveraging knowledge across phenotype-gene relationships
candidates.summary: Describes OMIM's curated catalogue of gene-phenotype relationships and allelic variants.
candidates.reason: Canonical OMIM reference; OMIM lists selected allelic variants only.

candidates.title: A corpus of GA4GH phenopackets: Case-level phenotyping for genomic diagnostics and discovery
candidates.summary: Phenopacket-store: thousands of case-level phenopackets curated from published case reports across hundreds of Mendelian diseases and genes.
candidates.reason: Shows that only a small share of published cases are in computable case-level form (phenopacket-store).

candidates.title: Rare disease variant curation from literature: assessing gaps with creatine transport deficiency in focus
candidates.summary: Manual curation of published SLC6A8 variants found only 53 of 185 literature variants present in ClinVar.
candidates.reason: Direct evidence that disease-causing variants published in the literature are missing from ClinVar.

candidates.title: Clinical variants paired with phenotype: A rich resource for brain gene curation
candidates.summary: Brain Gene Registry study in which 41.9% of 179 unique variants were absent from ClinVar at the time of submission.
candidates.reason: Further evidence of variant and phenotype data absent from ClinVar.

candidates.title: AVADA: toward automated pathogenic variant evidence retrieval directly from the full-text literature
candidates.summary: Automated full-text extraction recovered almost 60% of HGMD disease-causing variants and over 60,000 variants in HGMD but not in ClinVar.
candidates.reason: Shows the scale of literature variants not in ClinVar and prior automated attempts to close the gap.

candidates.title: Systematic reanalysis of clinical exome data yields additional diagnoses: implications for providers
candidates.summary: Reanalysis of 40 nondiagnostic exomes yielded 4 new diagnoses, driven by literature linking genes to phenotypes that was weak or not readily located at first analysis.
candidates.reason: Shows that diagnoses depend on literature evidence that is hard to find, i.e. the real-world cost of the gap.

candidates.title: Evaluating systematic reanalysis of clinical genomic data in rare disease from single center experience and literature review
candidates.summary: Single-centre reanalysis study with a literature review reporting a median 15% new diagnosis rate from reanalysis, largely from newly published gene-disease knowledge.
candidates.reason: Supports that newly published literature, not yet in databases, drives additional diagnoses.

candidates.title: Tracking genetic variants in the biomedical literature using LitVar 2.0
candidates.summary: LitVar 2.0 links genetic variants to the publications that mention them across PubMed and PMC.
candidates.reason: Shows variant knowledge lives in the literature and needs text mining to be found.

candidates.title: Standardizing variant naming in literature with VariantValidator to increase diagnostic rates
candidates.summary: Argues that non-standard variant descriptions in the literature hinder variant retrieval and diagnosis, and promotes VariantValidator-based standardization.
candidates.reason: Evidence that published variants are hard to reuse because of non-standard nomenclature.

candidates.title: The Human Phenotype Ontology: a tool for annotating and analyzing human hereditary disease
candidates.summary: Introduces the Human Phenotype Ontology for describing phenotypic abnormalities in human hereditary disease.
candidates.reason: Original HPO paper.

candidates.title: Deep phenotyping for precision medicine
candidates.summary: Defines deep phenotyping as precise, comprehensive analysis of phenotypic abnormalities using ontologies such as HPO.
candidates.reason: Canonical deep phenotyping reference.

candidates.title: The Human Phenotype Ontology in 2024: phenotypes around the world
candidates.summary: Current HPO update describing ontology growth, translations and annotation resources.
candidates.reason: Current HPO citation for the pinned HPO release.

candidates.title: The GA4GH Phenopacket schema defines a computable representation of clinical data
candidates.summary: Defines the GA4GH Phenopacket schema for exchanging case-level phenotype, genotype and disease data.
candidates.reason: Output format of the pipeline.

candidates.title: A corpus of GA4GH phenopackets: Case-level phenotyping for genomic diagnostics and discovery
candidates.summary: Phenopacket-store, a corpus of case-level phenopackets curated from the literature.
candidates.reason: Existing case-level resource the pilot diseases are absent from.

candidates.title: HGVS Recommendations for the Description of Sequence Variants: 2016 Update
candidates.summary: Current HGVS recommendations for describing DNA, RNA and protein sequence variants.
candidates.reason: Variant nomenclature standard.

candidates.title: HGVS Nomenclature 2024: improvements to community engagement, usability, and computability
candidates.summary: Describes the 2024 HGVS nomenclature update emphasising usability and computability.
candidates.reason: Most recent HGVS standard reference.

candidates.title: VariantValidator: Accurate validation, mapping, and formatting of sequence variation descriptions
candidates.summary: Introduces VariantValidator for validating and mapping HGVS variant descriptions between transcripts and genome builds.
candidates.reason: Normalization tool used in the pipeline.

candidates.title: A joint NCBI and EMBL-EBI transcript set for clinical genomics and research
candidates.summary: Introduces MANE, a matched set of representative transcripts agreed by NCBI and EMBL-EBI.
candidates.reason: Transcript standard (MANE Select) stated for every HGVS.

candidates.title: Standards and guidelines for the interpretation of sequence variants: a joint consensus recommendation of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology
candidates.summary: ACMG/AMP framework for classifying germline variants as pathogenic through benign using weighted evidence criteria.
candidates.reason: Canonical variant classification standard.

candidates.title: ClinGen--the Clinical Genome Resource
candidates.summary: Describes ClinGen, an NIH-funded resource to define the clinical relevance of genes and variants.
candidates.reason: Foundational variant curation infrastructure.

candidates.title: Mondo: integrating disease terminology across communities
candidates.summary: Describes the Mondo disease ontology, which integrates disease terminologies with cross-references to OMIM, Orphanet and others.
candidates.reason: Disease identifier standard (Mondo primary IDs).

section: Related Work: 2.1 Variant and phenotype extraction from the biomedical literature

candidates.title: An evaluation of GPT models for phenotype concept recognition
candidates.summary: Evaluates GPT models for HPO concept recognition from text against established tools.
candidates.reason: LLM HPO extraction evaluated against annotations, not databases.

candidates.title: Enhancing phenotype recognition in clinical notes using large language models: PhenoBCBERT and PhenoGPT
candidates.summary: Develops BERT- and GPT-based phenotype recognition on clinical notes, noting negation is not supported though negated findings can matter for diagnosis.
candidates.reason: Shows negation handling is a known gap; clinical notes not case reports.

candidates.title: Improving automated deep phenotyping through large language models using retrieval-augmented generation
candidates.summary: RAG-HPO evaluated on 120 published case reports with 1,792 manually assigned HPO terms, reaching F1 of 0.80 with Llama-3 70B versus Doc2Hpo, ClinPhen and FastHPOCR.
candidates.reason: Case-report benchmark for LLM HPO extraction scored against annotations.

candidates.title: Extraction of Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) Concepts from Clinical Notes Utilizing Large Language Models (LLM) with Model Context Protocol (MCP)
candidates.summary: Preprint evaluating LLMs with MCP-based grounding for HPO extraction, including separating patient from relative phenotypes and interpreting negated findings.
candidates.reason: Explicitly evaluates negation and patient attribution.

candidates.title: An artificial intelligence framework for end-to-end rare disease phenotyping from clinical notes using large language models
candidates.summary: RARE-PHENIX: LLM extraction, RAG-based HPO standardization and a ranking step, outperforming PhenoBERT on diagnostically relevant rare disease phenotypes.
candidates.reason: Recent rare-disease LLM phenotyping pipeline, evaluated on clinical notes.

candidates.title: PhenoTagger: a hybrid method for phenotype concept recognition using human phenotype ontology
candidates.summary: Hybrid dictionary and deep-learning HPO concept recognizer evaluated on annotated abstracts.
candidates.reason: Pre-LLM HPO recognition baseline on abstracts.

candidates.title: PhenoBERT: A Combined Deep Learning Method for Automated Recognition of Human Phenotype Ontology
candidates.summary: Deep-learning HPO recognition method combining CNN and BERT.
candidates.reason: Common HPO recognition baseline.

candidates.title: ClinPhen extracts and prioritizes patient phenotypes directly from medical records to expedite genetic disease diagnosis
candidates.summary: Rule-based HPO extraction from clinical notes with negation handling, prioritizing phenotypes for diagnosis.
candidates.reason: Clinical-note phenotype extractor with negation rules.

candidates.title: Doc2Hpo: a web application for efficient and accurate HPO concept curation
candidates.summary: Web application for semi-automated HPO curation from clinical text with negation detection.
candidates.reason: Tool with negation detection used as a baseline.

candidates.title: FastHPOCR: pragmatic, fast, and accurate concept recognition using the human phenotype ontology
candidates.summary: Fast HPO concept recognizer evaluated on annotated corpora.
candidates.reason: Recent HPO concept recognition baseline.

candidates.title: Enhancing human phenotype ontology term extraction through synthetic case reports and embedding-based retrieval: A novel approach for improved biomedical data annotation
candidates.summary: Uses synthetic case reports and embedding-based retrieval to improve HPO term extraction.
candidates.reason: Case-report-oriented HPO extraction method.

candidates.title: Structured Prompt Interrogation and Recursive Extraction of Semantics (SPIRES): a method for populating knowledge bases using zero-shot learning
candidates.summary: Zero-shot LLM method for extracting ontology-grounded structured knowledge from text.
candidates.reason: LLM structured extraction with ontology grounding, without per-value quotes.

candidates.title: Performance Characteristics of Reasoning Large Language Models for Evidence Extraction from Clinical Genomics Literature
candidates.summary: Preprint comparing reasoning LLMs on clinical genomics evidence extraction; counting probands (PS4) showed variable concordance, with Claude Sonnet 4 lowest.
candidates.reason: Shows LLM count fields are error-prone; an unfavourable result to report.

candidates.title: tmVar 3.0: an improved variant concept recognition and normalization tool
candidates.summary: Variant mention recognition and normalization tool for biomedical literature.
candidates.reason: Variant extraction baseline that outputs entities without patient-level phenotypes.

section: Related Work: 2.3 Case-level rare-disease resources, imperfect reference databases, and memorization

candidates.title: Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models
candidates.summary: Introduces Min-K% Prob, a reference-free method to detect whether text was in a model's pretraining data.
candidates.reason: Membership/memorization detection method (needs token probabilities).

candidates.title: Do Membership Inference Attacks Work on Large Language Models?
candidates.summary: Finds membership inference attacks barely beat random guessing on LLM pretraining data in many settings.
candidates.reason: Limits of membership inference as a memorization probe.

candidates.title: Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination in Large Language Models
candidates.summary: Black-box contamination detection via guided prompts asking a model to complete partial dataset instances, scored by overlap.
candidates.reason: Black-box completion probe usable on closed models.

candidates.title: Data Contamination Quiz: A Tool to Detect and Estimate Contamination in Large Language Models
candidates.summary: Detects verbatim contamination in black-box models by asking them to pick the original instance among perturbed options.
candidates.reason: Black-box probe usable without weights.

candidates.title: Data Contamination Through the Lens of Time
candidates.summary: Uses training cutoff dates as natural experiments to show performance drops on material published after the cutoff.
candidates.reason: Time-based contamination evidence relevant to published cases.

candidates.title: Benchmark Data Contamination of Large Language Models: A Survey
candidates.summary: Surveys benchmark data contamination in LLMs and detection and mitigation methods.
candidates.reason: Overview of contamination detection approaches.

candidates.title: LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Limited LLM Benchmark
candidates.summary: Benchmark with frequently updated questions from recent sources to limit contamination.
candidates.reason: Contamination mitigation by recency.

candidates.title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
candidates.summary: Shows that verbatim training sequences can be extracted from GPT-2 by querying the model.
candidates.reason: Foundational evidence of verbatim memorization.

candidates.title: Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models
candidates.summary: Shows memorization grows with model size, data duplication and prompt length.
candidates.reason: Foundational memorization quantification.

candidates.title: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
candidates.summary: Extracts training data from production black-box models including ChatGPT.
candidates.reason: Black-box memorization on closed models.

candidates.title: Memorization in Large Language Models in Medicine: Prevalence, Characteristics, and Implications
candidates.summary: Finds memorization prevalent in medical LLM adaptation, higher than in the general domain, and categorizes it as beneficial, uninformative or harmful.
candidates.reason: Medical-domain memorization evidence.

candidates.title: Simulating Viva Voce Examinations to Evaluate Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Models
candidates.summary: Clinical reasoning benchmark built from published case reports that probes memorization by asking models to continue a case report's first sentence (following Golchin et al.).
candidates.reason: Memorization probe applied to published case reports.

candidates.title: MedicalAgentsBench for Complex Medical Reasoning: Comparing Internalized Reasoning Models versus Externalized Agent-based Frameworks
candidates.summary: Includes a Levenshtein-similarity memorization check (MELD) on medical benchmark items, noting absence of a match does not prove clean data.
candidates.reason: Biomedical black-box memorization check and its limits.

candidates.title: OpenAlex: A fully-open index of scholarly works, authors, venues, institutions, and concepts
candidates.summary: Introduces OpenAlex, a fully open index of scholarly works, authors, venues, institutions and concepts available via API and data dump.
candidates.reason: Primary paper introducing OpenAlex.

section: 3. Methodology - 3.5 Held-out ground truth, pre-registration and outcomes

candidates.title: THE USE OF CONFIDENCE OR FIDUCIAL LIMITS ILLUSTRATED IN THE CASE OF THE BINOMIAL
candidates.summary: Derives exact confidence limits for a binomial proportion (Biometrika 26:404-413).
candidates.reason: Original Clopper-Pearson exact interval used for audit and gatekeeper shares.

section: 4. Experiments - 4.7 O3: gap candidates awaiting adjudication

candidates.title: The mutational constraint spectrum quantified from variation in 141,456 humans
candidates.summary: Introduces the gnomAD dataset of 141,456 exomes and genomes and a loss-of-function constraint metric.
candidates.reason: Primary gnomAD paper; population frequency (PM2) left to the panel.
